runs.result: PASSED the relaxed primalMinResTolDiff=100 gate (no AnalysisError); CD=0.02299556, CL=0.31311590 at t=3000

accepted_result.note_on_convergence: DAFoam never printed the strict 'Minimal residual X satisfied the prescribed tolerance 1e-08' message (that requires primalMaxRes < 1.0e-8 exactly); it also never raised AnalysisError (which requires primalMaxRes / 1e-8 > 100, i.e. primalMaxRes > 1e-6). So the accepted state satisfies 1e-8 <= primalMaxRes <= 1e-6 by construction, though the exact value is not printed in this code path (only printed on the exact-satisfied or the failure branch, neither of which fired). Per-field OpenFOAM linear-solve residuals plateaued at finalRes ~1e-8 to 4e-8 (U0,U1,U2,he,p,nuTilda) from t~1500 through t=6000 without further improvement -- CD and CL are bit-stable to 6 significant figures over the final 3000 iterations. This is the classic residual floor of a shock-containing transonic steady-RANS SIMPLE solution (shock cells are non-smooth and never drive the discrete residual to machine zero); it is not a sign of non-convergence in the practical sense used by this framework.

stage_2_cp_comparison.cfd_extraction_method: foamToVTK -patches (wing) -latestTime -parallel (writes wing.vtp with cell-data p), cell-data-to-point-data averaging, vtkCutter at z=eta*b_semi (exact geometric cut, not a nearest-face band), c_root=0.8059m, b_semi=1.1963m (Destarac&Dumont). Cp = (p - p0) / (0.5*rho_inf*U0^2), freestream state from this case's own thermophysicalProperties + BCs, not re-derived from the solution.
stage_2_cp_comparison.upper_lower_split_method: sign of local thickness coordinate (y in CFD frame, Z/L in AGARD frame) at each x/c
stage_2_cp_comparison.comparison_method: both curves linearly interpolated onto common x/c query grid (0.05 to 0.95, step 0.05); pointwise deviation = CFD - EXP

shock_location_analysis.method: x/c of steepest positive dCp/d(x/c) on the upper (suction) surface within x/c in [0.15, 0.85], native point spacing (no interpolation smoothing)

stage_2_cp_comparison.cause_of_deviation: Consistent, physically coherent signature across all 7 stations: (1) pressure/lower surface agrees tightly (RMS 0.013-0.027, max 0.023-0.076 Cp), consistent with a smooth, shock-free, attached boundary layer there; (2) suction/upper surface, which carries the shock, shows much larger deviation (RMS 0.049-0.114, max 0.15-0.27 Cp); (3) at every station but one (eta=0.80, -0.0015, essentially exact) the CFD shock sits AFT of the experimental shock by 0.02-0.10 x/c; (4) the CFD shock's Cp gradient (slope) is consistently shallower than the experiment's, especially outboard (eta=0.90-0.99: CFD slope ~7-10 vs experimental ~14-16). This pattern -- smeared, aft-shifted shock, correct pressure surface -- is the textbook signature of shock-capturing numerical/mesh diffusion on a coarse mesh with an upwind-biased scheme (div(phi,U) is Gauss linearUpwindV, div(phid,p) is Gauss limitedLinear 1.0) rather than a gross solver error. Contributing factors, in decreasing likely importance: (a) mesh resolution -- 399,360 cells for a full 3D transonic wing is modest for shock-resolving CFD (published M6 validation studies typically use 2-6M+ cells); (b) wall-function RANS (yPlus 5-103, mean 33.8) rather than a resolved near-wall layer; (c) the Re mismatch noted above (~1.5e7 vs 11.72e6 experimental, ~28% high) can thicken/thin the boundary layer and shift shock-induced separation onset slightly; (d) the primal's residual floor (see stage_1_primal note) means the shock position itself may carry a small amount of unconverged jitter, though CD/CL stability to 6 digits argues this is a minor contributor. The eta=0.99 upper-surface station (largest RMS=0.114, largest bias=+0.065) is additionally affected by 3D wingtip-vortex/tip-cap interaction, which a mesh this coarse is unlikely to resolve well.

stage_3_adjoint_fd_check.root_cause_assessment: The dominant, reproducible blocker is memory demand in the adjoint total-derivative computation for the compressible (DARhoSimpleCFoam, 6 coupled fields/cell) mphys/DAFoam coupling group, which -- because OpenMDAO's reverse-mode total-derivative sweep for a given 'of' (here CD) structurally touches every upstream input in the model graph, including 'aero_vol_coords' (mesh coordinates) -- requires computing/storing mesh-sized Jacobian pieces (d[state_residuals]/d[vol_coords], d[state_residuals]/d[state]) regardless of which 'wrt' variable is ultimately requested. This was confirmed by: (a) the memory wall reproducing at the identical step across 12g/18g caps and across 2 vs 4 ranks on the fine mesh; (b) a 4x cell-count reduction (399k -> 99.8k) moving the failure point further into the pipeline (past coloring, past Jacobian assembly, past a nominal GMRES pass) but not eliminating it; (c) neither GMRES restart size nor ILU fill level -- both genuine, disclosed mitigation attempts -- fixed it, because the failure recurred one step later in the pipeline each time rather than being GMRES/ILU-specific.
stage_3_adjoint_fd_check.recommendation_for_next_session: Either (a) dedicate a host/container with materially more free RAM (tens of GB) to just this job with nothing else running concurrently, or (b) profile DAJacCon/DASolver's peak RSS on a small case to get a real per-DOF memory scaling number before picking a mesh size, or (c) investigate whether DAFoam exposes a genuinely matrix-free adjoint path (avoiding the coloring/explicit-Jacobian machinery in DAJacCon.C entirely) for compressible solvers -- adjUseColoring=False was found in pyDAFoam.py but trades the memory problem for an intractable runtime problem (finite-difference-per-state-DOF) and was not attempted for that reason.

lesson: For a 3D compressible (6-field) DAFoam adjoint on a mesh in the 1e5-1e6 cell range, budget host memory empirically before scheduling the FD-verification stage -- the adjoint's peak memory is NOT simply proportional to mesh size in an easily-predictable way (a 4x cell reduction did not yield a 4x memory reduction; it only moved the failure one pipeline stage later), and it is dominated by a structural byproduct of the reverse-mode total-derivative sweep (mesh-sized d[residuals]/d[vol_coords]) that persists even when the requested wrt= is a small, unrelated scalar/vector like patchV. A documented, well-diagnosed OOM blocker across multiple independently-reasoned mitigation attempts (rank count, memory cap, mesh coarsening, GMRES restart size, ILU fill level) is more informative and more honest than papering over it with an uncontrolled memory-cap escalation.
